tagline: Up the shore of Lake Superior to the Pigeon River.
intro: Out of Duluth the old road, County 61, keeps close to the water as far as Two Harbors. From there Highway 61 carries on up the North Shore along the foot of the Sawtooth Range, past cliffs and state parks, with the lake to the southeast all the way. After Two Harbors there is no town for almost 30 miles. Then come Beaver Bay, the oldest settlement on the shore, Silver Bay, Tofte, Lutsen and Grand Marais, and at last Grand Portage near the border.
When Split Rock Lighthouse went up in 1910, there was no road to it at all. So many excursion boats came to look that one was built in 1924. That road is now Highway 61.

moments.title: Gooseberry Falls State Park
moments.text: From the highway bridge you can count three layers of old lava flow, cut through by the Gooseberry River on its way down Upper, Middle and Lower Falls to the lake.

moments.title: Split Rock Lighthouse
moments.text: Built on a 133-foot cliff after the Mataafa Storm of 1905, retired in 1969, it is lit again every November 10 for the Edmund Fitzgerald.

moments.title: Grand Portage National Monument
moments.text: Voyageurs carried their fur bundles 8.5 miles here around the falls of the Pigeon River, on the path long known as Gichi-onigaming, the Great Carrying Place.
